findings.claim: Q5's WHY-DISTRACTORS defends the key against option C with a checkably false statement about the passage: it says Quilvey's readier position is "offered in her own voice", but Quilvey has no direct speech anywhere in the text. Every Quilvey sentence is the writer's own narration, which is the one place a complaining C-picker has a foothold. The same misdescription is repeated in generator_meta.self_blind_solve.
findings.evidence: Q5 rationale, shipped file: "C = role_or_attribution_swap – Quilvey's readiness to use a matched phage as a standard option is her position, offered in her own voice and immediately fenced by her own limit; the writer reports it without joining it." Programmatic scan of every curly-quotation span in the shipped passage returns exactly two, both Bellinghast: 'Our results suggest that phages add something in a subset of these infections,' and 'They cannot tell us how large that something is.' The entire Quilvey block is the writer's sentence: "Josephine Quilvey, who treats bone and joint infection at one of the four hospitals, is readier than that. She would offer a matched phage as a standard option in infected joint replacements, where the alternative is often a second operation to take the implant out, and she is deliberate about the limit: she means that setting, not resistant infection at large." generator_meta.self_blind_solve repeats it: "Q5/C by Quilvey's own voice and limit". Diff of candidates-final-round1 vs candidates-final shows passage and all twenty option strings are byte-identical between rounds and only q3.rat plus four metadata strings were touched, so this defect was carried into the shipping file unrepaired.
findings.why: Rationale factual accuracy about the text is the pedagogy stage's own probe, and this is a false claim inside the teaching payload for the unit's hardest item — the stance question whose whole discrimination is voice attribution. It does not flip the key: C stays defeated by three writer-owned judgments I verified verbatim in the passage — "which is worth saying before any of the numbers that follow", "the care is warranted: without a comparison group, a recovery in a patient taking four drugs says little about the fifth", and "that trial, not any series, will decide whether the treatment becomes ordinary" — each flatly incompatible with C's "should already be a standard option". Because the recorded pedagogy verdict is MINOR_FIXES rather than CLEAR, an outstanding minor rationale fix is what that verdict already asserts, so this confirms rather than refutes it. Accurate replacement: "attributed to her and fenced by her own limit", which is also the stronger defense because it survives the student who notices that only Bellinghast is quoted.

findings.claim: Q1's key and Q5's key share the authored 4-gram "the results so far", a string that occurs in no distractor anywhere in the unit and nowhere in the passage. Two of the five keys therefore carry a private lexical fingerprint the wrong answers do not, and the integrated cross-question sweep records no disposition of it.
findings.evidence: Q1/C (key) = "How phages are matched to particular infections, and how far the results so far reach." Q5/B (key) = "Interested, but unwilling to let the results so far settle the question." Programmatic check on the shipped file: 'the results so far' appears in exactly those two option strings and in no other option in any of the five questions; passage.lower().count('results so far') = 0 — the passage's only nearby wording is Bellinghast's quoted "Our results suggest that phages add something in a subset of these infections". This is invisible to M-TELL, which measures option length rather than shared lexis; I re-ran the length check and confirm the metadata's corrected M-TELL claim is accurate (key is the strict-longest option in Q3 only, A=89 vs C=85 characters, and is never the longest in Q1, Q2, Q4 or Q5).
findings.why: A key-to-key echo is exactly what integrated review's cross-question row exists to catch: G-STEM judges one item blind at a time, G-KEY judges one item against the passage, and neither can see a string shared across two keys. Severity is minor rather than major because the shared string is an evaluative hedge frame rather than answer content, exploiting it requires having already solved Q1, and the unit's own generator_meta already discloses the adjacent Law-10 hedge residual ("The key carries the qualifying phrase in all five questions") as an accepted, adjudicated tell. It is a real unrecorded property of the shipped unit and is consistent with the recorded MINOR_NOTES verdict, not a refutation of it.
